name: cua_get_api_reference
title: Computer use API reference
description: Return the complete `cua` API reference that every cua_run_code program must follow: methods, signatures, and operating rules. Call it before the first cua_run_code program of a conversation, and again whenever the reference is no longer in your context or a program fails on an unknown `cua` method. It only reads: nothing on the desktop or in the program environment changes.

name: cua_run_code
title: Computer use program
description: Run a TypeScript program to observe and operate desktop applications. The global cua object is ready to use; retain application and window objects across calls. Only tools.cua is available inside the program. Call other session tools directly. Use inspect(...values) to display selected text and images. The program contains TypeScript REPL statements; only erasable syntax is accepted, with no enum or namespaces. Type annotations are advisory. Top-level declarations and await are supported; top-level return is not supported. Use inspect(...values) to display output. Do not use console. The program runs in strict mode: assigning an undeclared name throws, so use globalThis for intentional globals; eval and new Function are unavailable. Variables, functions, and imported modules remain in memory for this Agent across calls. Each call runs one program in its own top-level scope. Its top-level let, const, var, class, and function declarations, and the names it received from earlier programs, are copied into the top-level scope of later programs: later programs receive copies of these variables, not references to them, so an object they hold is still shared. In one program, either use a copied name or declare it again; do not declare a name and also use its copied value. Assigning to a copied name, even one declared with const, changes only this program's copy, which later programs receive. Do not declare var inside blocks; a block-level var changes which value later programs copy. Functions and still-running code from earlier programs keep the values they captured, and assignments they make later are not copied; keep shared mutable state in objects. If a program fails before a declaration of an existing name finishes, later programs keep that name's earlier value. Use await import(...) for modules; require and module are unavailable. Relative import specifiers resolve from the working directory of this environment's first program, while process.cwd() and relative file paths follow each program's working directory. Direct filesystem access follows the environment's launch-time sandbox policy; process.env starts empty. Timeout and cancellation results say whether retained variables were preserved or cleared. Restart, sandbox changes, output overflow, or process failure clears them. Recreate missing variables and resources; conversation history does not restore state. Earlier mutations and tool effects are not rolled back. Approved sandbox escalations use a fresh environment and discard its variables afterward. Await tools and cleanup before the program ends; unfinished tools reject. After completion, timeout, or cancellation, new tool calls are rejected and captured output is discarded; background work may still change state. Await child-process completion before the program ends; raw output belongs to the active evaluation. Each program starts in the Session's current directory. Running programs keep their initial directory. A sandbox escalation approves this complete program for one execution only. Nested tools retain their own policies and approvals. Request wider access only after evidence of a denial. Earlier effects may already have completed: inspect them before explicitly retrying. Programs are never replayed automatically.

code.description: The TypeScript program to execute, following this tool's execution instructions.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this program does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "Count TODO markers across packages"; "Read failing test and its fixture"; "Rename config key in every cordis.yml".

timeoutMs.description: Positive elapsed-time budget in milliseconds, including nested tool and approval waits. Default 120000; capped at 600000. Zero does not disable the deadline.

name: cua_reset
title: Reset computer use program state
description: Discard the program environment of this connection: every variable, import, and application or window object held by earlier cua_run_code calls. A running cua_run_code program is cancelled. Application access grants and the desktop applications themselves are unaffected; the next cua_run_code call starts a fresh environment. Use it when the environment has become unusable or its retained state must not carry into the next task.
